title: Effect of a two-ended action
statement: Let $L>0$, let $q,q'$ be optional states, let $u,v$ be tape contents indexed by the integers, let $h$ be an integer head position, and let $a,b$ be optional writes and $d\in\{-1,0,1\}$ a displacement. Applying the two-ended action to the configuration with tape contents $u,v$ at the two ends, all intermediate tapes blank, and both end heads at $h$ gives the corresponding configuration in state $q'$, with the end cells at $h$ changed according to the writes and the heads at $h+d$. An absent write leaves that cell unchanged; a present write may place either a Boolean symbol or a blank, while the input-head position and empty output remain as in the two-ended configuration.
replaced:
Let $L > 0$, and consider a two-ended configuration on $L + 1$ work tapes whose
tape zero holds $u$ and whose last tape holds $v$, with common head position $h$.
Applying the two-ended action with optional writes $a$, $b$, displacement $d$ and
next state $q'$ yields the two-ended configuration in state $q'$ whose tape zero is
$u$ with cell $h$ overwritten by $a$ (if $a$ writes), whose last tape is $v$ with
cell $h$ overwritten by $b$ (if $b$ writes), and whose common head position is
$h + d$; the input head and the empty output are unchanged.
